history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed (Buddhist monastery). Established around 1730 by the Ngadakpa (Nyadakpa) Lama above the twin villages of Rinchenpong and Kaluk; described as the third oldest monastery in Sikkim, founded with around 98 lamas. Noted for a rare statue of Ati Buddha (Adi-Buddha) in the Yab-Yum position. Serves as a training centre for lamas. Also called Sang Ngag Yangtse Monastery (Govt of Sikkim, Soreng district site). Do not confuse with the 1996 Rinchen Choling Tamu Monastery near Rinchenpong Bazaar (Nyingma, Gurung Buddhist Society) — different monastery. Sect sources differ slightly: Lonely Planet gives Zurmang Kagyu. District flag: now in Soreng district; older sources say West Sikkim/Gyalshing. CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name 'Rinchenpong' — corrected to Sikkim. Coordinates 27.2353, 88.2685 corroborated by Wikipedia and aroundus.

name: Rinchenpong Monastery
town_description: Rinchenpong is a hill town in West Sikkim at about 1,700 m, near Kaluk, about 123 km west of Gangtok. It is known for its monasteries, trekking routes, the historic Poison Pokhri (Bikh Pokhri) lake, and panoramic views of Mt. Kangchenjunga.

travel.airport: Nearest airport: Bagdogra (IXB), about 130–135 km (4–5 hrs by road). Pakyong Airport is closer (~105 km) but flights are infrequent.
travel.road: 3–4 hrs from Gangtok by hired or shared cab; reached from Rinchenpong bazaar by a mountain trail/stone steps (~1.2 km); about 46 km from Pelling.

visitor_information.best_time: Dry season — October–May, when trails are accessible and mountain views are clear.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify); generally open in daylight hours. Photography inside the sanctum has reportedly been restricted recently.
